title: Mapping Heat by Bicycle
transcript: One afternoon, two cyclists left the same weather station and rode in opposite directions, each carrying a temperature sensor in a ventilated shield. A city research team wanted to know how much heat pedestrians encountered away from the station, which stood on an open lawn. The riders covered the same streets on several clear days and swapped routes halfway through the survey to check whether differences followed the streets or the equipment. A row of apartment blocks without trees repeatedly came out warmer than a shaded street nearby. The hottest spot shifted later in the day as building shadows crossed the road. City planners used the findings to choose where to test shade structures at bus stops and when to measure their effect.

questions.prompt: Why did the cyclists swap routes during the survey?
options: To finish both routes before the roads became busy
To see whether temperature differences were due to location or equipment
To find out which route had fewer shaded stretches
To make both riders travel the same total distance
questions.answer: To see whether temperature differences were due to location or equipment
questions.explanation: 交换路线可以检验温差是随街道位置变化，还是随测量设备变化。

questions.prompt: What should planners infer when deciding how to evaluate shade at bus stops?
options: An open lawn is the best place to test a shelter.
Sensors should always stay with the same rider.
Temperature readings from the nearest street can replace measurements at a stop.
Measurements at different times can matter because local shade changes.
questions.answer: Measurements at different times can matter because local shade changes.
questions.explanation: 阴影随时间移动，导致最热位置改变，因此评估站点遮阴效果时需要考虑测量时段。
